claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for release now, based on aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, with residual-risk notation despite an unresolved named-segment evaluation gap and an open legal disclosure question.
decision_criteria: A compliant certification would require admissible evidence that the named-segment gap is either resolved, not material under policy, or covered by an approved risk acceptance.
A pending legal disclosure question must be closed or formally covered before certification can be treated as policy-supported.
Aggregate readiness and rehearsal results can support readiness, but they cannot substitute for the missing materiality and disclosure determinations.
Public governance guidance may support residual-risk framing, but internal policy controls the certification decision in this case.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying evidence for the 2.5 percentage-point aggregate readiness pass and the 1.1 percentage-point named-segment miss.
Provide the partner launch checklist showing the affected segment is a named launch use case.
Provide the full internal release policy and any approval workflow governing disclosure or risk acceptance for material limitations.
Provide the current legal-review artifact or disposition on whether disclosure is required.
Provide any approved risk-acceptance record, if one exists, covering this specific gap.
specific_concerns: The policy text says materiality is triggered by a named launch use case; the actor summary says the affected segment is named in a partner launch checklist.
Legal review on disclosure is still open, and the policy text says pending legal review prevents product labeling from resolving materiality.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not by themselves resolve whether a named-segment gap is material or whether disclosure/risk acceptance is required.

The actor relies on public governance guidance about documenting limitations and monitoring residual risk, but that does not establish satisfaction of the specific internal policy predicate for certification.
Evidence access is limited to the actor summary only, so there is no direct admissible record of the underlying metrics, checklist language, policy artifact, or legal-review status.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify the model now is not fully supported because the required materiality/disclosure predicate remains unresolved on the present record.
Any implication that the named-segment gap is immaterial or adequately covered is unsupported from the admissible evidence provided here.
Any implication that public framework guidance independently authorizes release under the internal policy is unsupported.
